subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should `gateway.security.*` govern every Gateway WebSocket upgrade before plugin routing, or only the core Gateway protocol server?
rationale: The current hook enforces only the fallback core server, while the config names and help text describe gateway-level upgrade hardening; choosing the protected boundary determines both safe placement and the user-facing contract.

options.title: Use one Gateway-wide pre-upgrade boundary
options.body: Run the shared policy before plugin routing and use the current config snapshot, with explicit documented exemptions only where a plugin protocol cannot safely share the policy.

options.title: Make this core-protocol-only
options.body: Retain the core server hook but rename and document the settings as applying only to the core Gateway protocol so plugin routes are not implied to be covered.

recommendation.title: Use one Gateway-wide pre-upgrade boundary
recommendation.body: Run the shared policy before plugin routing and use the current config snapshot, with explicit documented exemptions only where a plugin protocol cannot safely share the policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly requests this Gateway security-boundary decision from this reviewer, and the choice affects public configuration semantics.
